description: A parent needs to make sure a child's school, after-school program, and pediatrician all have the same understanding of a recurring health issue, including symptom triggers, accommodations, and what to do if it flares up.

user_profile.persona: 40-year-old parent managing both medical and school communication
user_profile.context: Recent confusion showed that each adult only knows part of the child's situation
user_profile.communication_style: Clear and protective, wants consistent wording across settings

fact_sheet.fact: The child's full name is Leo Miller.
Leo Miller's date of birth is May 15, 2016.
Leo Miller is diagnosed with Exercise-Induced Bronchospasm with Allergic Triggers (ICD-10 Code: J45.901).
The diagnosis was formally documented by Dr. Anya Sharma at Riverbend Pediatric Associates on September 2, 2023.
A primary environmental trigger is outdoor air temperature below 50°F (10°C).
A known allergic trigger is airborne pollen from freshly cut grass.
Inhaling strong chemical odors, specifically from bleach-based cleaning products, will trigger symptoms.
The initial symptom of a flare-up is a persistent, dry cough.
During a flare-up, an audible high-pitched wheezing sound occurs when Leo exhales.
Leo is prescribed an Albuterol Sulfate inhaler, brand name ProAir HFA.
The standard dosage is two actuations (puffs), totaling 180 mcg, administered via a spacer device.
The inhaler must be administered 15 minutes prior to strenuous physical activity, including school P.E. class.
Leo's pediatrician is Dr. Anya Sharma at Riverbend Pediatric Associates, reachable at 555-876-5432.
The school nurse at Maple Creek Elementary is Ms. Carol Dane, whose office phone is 555-112-2334.
The director of the Bright Horizons Kids Club is Mr. James Finch, contactable at 555-998-8776.
Leo's school, Maple Creek Elementary, must provide indoor recess when the local Air Quality Index (AQI) exceeds 100.
Per Leo's 504 Plan dated October 1, 2023, his classroom (Room 204) must only be cleaned with fragrance-free, non-bleach products.
Staff at the Bright Horizons Kids Club are required to supervise Leo's use of his inhaler before outdoor playground activities.
If Leo exhibits shortness of breath that does not improve within 5 minutes of using the inhaler, call 911.
The primary emergency contact is Sarah Miller (mother) at 555-234-5678.
The secondary emergency contact is Robert Miller (father) at 555-234-5679.
At Maple Creek Elementary, Leo's inhaler (Serial #: AXD4588B) and spacer are stored in a labeled bin in the nurse's office medication cabinet.
At Bright Horizons Kids Club, a separate inhaler is kept in a red zippered pouch labeled 'Leo Miller' inside the front desk first-aid kit.
A central Google Doc named 'Leo Miller Health Coordination Plan' contains all official information.
The 'view-only' share link for the health plan was distributed to all key contacts via email on November 5, 2023.
All modifications to the plan are logged in the 'Revision History' section of the document, initialed and dated by Sarah Miller.

The health coordination plan includes Leo's symptom triggers, medication and flare-up response steps, school and after-school accommodations, emergency contacts, and storage locations for inhalers and spacers.
On November 6, 2023, Sarah Miller received acknowledgments from the school nurse, the Kids Club director, and Leo's parents confirming they had reviewed the shared health plan.
